# Compact language usage index

<!-- Generated by coverage/usage-index.ts. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every name the Compact language offers, and where a `test-contracts` fixture uses it. The names are read from the compiler, so anything added there appears here on the next run — whether or not a fixture exists for it.

This is the counterpart to `./compiler/go`, which measures the compiler's own code. That number cannot distinguish a covered standard-library circuit from an uncovered one, because they compile through identical code.

Scanned the **101 fixtures** in `test-contracts/`. Nothing else. A name listed as uncovered may still be exercised by the e2e suite, which compiles contracts out of `examples/` — so read this as a to-do list for this suite, not as a claim about the repository.

## What this does and does not show

- **Used is not tested.** A usage site proves a fixture mentions the name. Whether it is meaningfully exercised depends on that fixture's assertions.
- **Names are matched as words**, after comments and string literals are removed. A local variable sharing a standard-library name would still count.
- **Generic instantiations are not separated** — `some<Field>` and `some<Bytes<32>>` are one entry.
